newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Gold oversold, may test resistance.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Gold oversold, may test resistance.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
-----------------VIEWS FROM THE MARKET - July 11 -------------
Gold reamins heavily oversold and may make a move on $320.00 resistance on Friday, though the longer term outlook is seen extremely vulnerable to the downside, traders and chartists said.
Silver will follow the gyrations of gold, while palladium and platinum will attempt to consolidate despite dealer confirmation that shipments have reached Japan.
GOLD - With the 14-day RSI still in oversold territory at around 25 percent several traders suggest prices may move to test resistance above $320.00 on Friday.
However longer term outlooks remained bearish after prices plunged to a 12-year low of $313,60 early this week.
"At the moment we are seeing the obvious knee jerk reaction to the recent strong downside pressure, though I think present levels in the long run will be hard to maintain," one trader said.
Currently there is support at $315.00, a level the market has held over the last few days.
A breach of this level would see a retest of the 12-year low and possibly $300.00.
If gold managed to break above $320.00 traders expect resistance to emerge between $322.50 and $323.00.
Referring to the August gold contract Martin Squires of Rudolf Wolff said, "We continue to look for the successful negotiation of $322.00/$325.00 before developing confidence in a trend reversal."
At 0700 GMT spot gold was quoted at $320.00321.10, against Thursday's London close of $319.40/$319.90.
SILVER - Short-covering is likely to hold prices well above support at $4.25 an ounce, though any sudden movement in gold would swiftly impact on silver, traders said.
Medium term resistance is expected at $4.57 and $4.62.
At 0700 GMT spot silver was quoted at $4.37/4.39, versus $4.33/$4.35.
PLATINUM - Seen continuing to build a base around $395.00 and eyeing higher levels above $400.00 after absorbing confirmation of renewed Russian supplies to Japan.
Below $395 next support is seen at $390, while stiff overhead resistance is pegged at the July 8 high of $410.00
At 0700 GMT spot platinum was quoted at $399.00/402.00, against $396.00/$400.00.
